data.title: Molluscum contagiosum extraction
data.summary: Physical removal of molluscum bodies by expression or curettage
data.body:
Molluscum contagiosum is a poxvirus infection that usually resolves on its own over months to a couple of years. Treatment shortens the course, reduces spread and autoinoculation, and helps with itching or cosmetic concern. Physical extraction is quick, cheap and effective in a cooperative patient.

## Indications
- Few to moderate lesions in children or adults
- Genital molluscum in adults (sexually transmitted; screen partner)
- Lesions spreading by scratching, or with molluscum dermatitis
- Patient or parent preference for active treatment

## Contraindications
- Very young or uncooperative child with many lesions (consider topical KOH or cantharidin, or watchful waiting)
- Inflamed lesions (BOTE sign) — these are resolving; leave them
- Lesions on the eyelid margin (refer to ophthalmology)
- Bleeding disorder (relative)

## Pre-procedure
- Consent: brief pain, pinpoint bleeding, small pitted scars, new lesions may still appear
- **Adults with many, large or facial lesions: test for HIV** and consider other immunosuppression
- Topical anaesthetic (lidocaine–prilocaine) under occlusion for 45–60 minutes in children; respect the maximum area for age
- Count and map the lesions

## Equipment
- Comedone extractor, fine curette, or 26G needle
- Fine forceps
- Povidone-iodine or spirit, gauze, gloves
- Antibiotic ointment, small dressings

## Procedure step by step
1. Clean with antiseptic.
2. **Expression**: make a tiny nick in the umbilicated centre with the needle; press the extractor loop around the papule until the white, cheesy molluscum body comes out.
3. **Curettage**: stabilise the skin and remove the papule with one quick scoop of a small curette.
4. **Endpoint**: the whole core is out and only a small, clean, bleeding crater remains.
5. Dab the base with povidone-iodine (some apply 10% KOH or phenol to the base; do so carefully).
6. Press for haemostasis.
7. Treat all visible lesions in one session if tolerated; small ones may be missed, so re-examine carefully.

## Post-procedure care
- Keep clean; apply antibiotic ointment for 2–3 days
- Avoid scratching, shaving or waxing over affected areas
- Do not share towels; avoid shared baths and pools until clear
- Treat molluscum dermatitis with emollients and mild topical steroid

## Complications & management
- Bleeding: pressure
- Secondary infection: topical antibiotic
- Pitted scar or PIH: sunscreen; usually fades
- New lesions: from incubation (up to 6 weeks); treat at review
- Anxiety in children: use distraction; stop if not tolerated

## Sessions & follow-up
- Review every 3–4 weeks and treat new lesions
- Usually 2–3 sessions
- Genital cases: screen for other STIs
